title: The ants did dig tunnels — the question is why you cannot see them
question: In which of these can you point at a tunnel? If neither, say neither — that is the useful answer and it tells me the fix is contrast, not light.
context_md:
You said of the earlier cards: *\"I don't see tunnels\"*, *\"These look identical\"*, *\"looks like the whole corner is going away\"*. You were reading the pictures correctly, and I can now say what is in them.

**There is a real nest in this bank.** A connected-component pass over the standing hollow — the measurement that separates one gallery from a scatter of bites — says **91-96% of all enclosed void sits in ONE connected run of 134-165 cells**, with 0-2 isolated single cells, across three seeds. It is a gallery, not nibbling. Both pictures below contain the same one.

**Why it does not show.** I measured what the renderer actually puts on screen for each thing in the bank. The tunnel interior is the only thing in the scene with no colour of its own: it ranges from near-black to nearly sky-bright (30 to 150 of 255) depending how far it is from the entrance, because a shallow tunnel with an open mouth genuinely gets daylight down it. Correct light, unreadable picture.

**Two things I checked so you don't have to wonder.** Making the lighting finer does not help — I ran it at exact per-cell light and the tunnels got *brighter*, not darker. And I tried twice to make the ants dig differently (prefer buried ground; prefer ground with a roof on it), swept both across their whole range, and both made the nest *worse*. The digging behaviour is not the problem.

**What I think is left**, and I would rather you told me than have me guess: the only thing in the whole scene that reads as separable from the bank is the packed wall the ants leave, and it clears the bank's own mottle by a hair (9 of 255 against a mottle of 8). Everything else overlaps. If neither picture below works for you, the answer is that the tunnel *wall* has to carry the whole signal and it needs real contrast, not a slightly darker brown.
